turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would do as she instructed, but he could not bear the thought of life without her, and that he would struggle to provide for their son and carry on her legacy.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told Wang Lung that he would do everything his mother instructed, and that he would be strong for his father and take care of the household as she had taught him.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked if there was anything she could do for her mother-in-law, her voice barely above a whisper.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the maid to take care of the household and cook the evening meal, as she would not be able to do it herself.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung asked O-lan to tell him what she wanted to see happen before she passed on, and what she expected of their son's future

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told his father that he would stay by his side and take care of him, just as their mother would have wanted

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked her husband if he was feeling better after the conversation with their mother

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she wanted to see their son married and settled, with a good wife and a prosperous life, before she passed on, her voice barely above a whisper.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung insisted that their son's future was secure, and that he would make sure O-lan's wishes were fulfilled, before he took his leave to oversee the evening meal.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: the eldest son told Wang Lung that he would make sure to get married soon, as his mother had wished, and that he would find a good wife who would take care of his father when she was no longer there

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked O-lan if there was anything she needed, and if she could get her some water or a warm blanket

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son if he had given any more thought to finding a suitable bride, her eyes locking onto his with a determined gaze.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung scolded the eldest son, telling him that he had been dawdling long enough and that he should find a bride as soon as possible, for his mother's sake.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son smiled reassuringly and told his mother that he had indeed given more thought to finding a suitable bride, and he had been thinking of a young woman from a neighboring village who was known for her kindness and hard work.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: the maid asked O-lan if she would like some tea, as it might be easier to drink than water, and if she could get her a small cup

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked the eldest son if he had made any progress in speaking with the young woman from the neighboring village, her eyes searching for reassurance that their future was secure.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung demanded to know why the eldest son had not yet spoken with the young woman, and insisted that he must bring her to meet their mother as soon as possible.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told Wang Lung that he would speak with the young woman from the neighboring village as soon as possible, and that he would bring her to meet their mother as soon as she was able to receive visitors.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told Wang Lung that perhaps it would be best to wait a little while before bringing the young woman to meet their mother, as she was still not feeling well.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at the maid with a tired expression and asked her to bring her a small cloth to wipe her lips, which were dry and cracked from thirst

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
